questions.question: Why can BM25 miss a document about automobile repair for the query `car mechanic`?
options: It scores lexical evidence and does not inherently equate `car` with `automobile`
It always removes the rarest query term before scoring
It represents every document with one learned semantic vector
It requires documents and queries to have equal token counts

questions.question: Which change addresses simple morphological variation more directly than semantic mismatch?
options: Adding an approximate vector index
Applying stemming or lemmatization in the analyzer
Increasing every document length
Removing inverse document frequency

questions.question: A support query describes a symptom while the relevant article names its cause. Which retrieval weakness is most likely?
options: The query has too many exact identifiers

The vector index contains too many dimensions

questions.question: Why can broad synonym expansion reduce precision?
options: It prevents every exact match from scoring

It can add unintended senses of ambiguous terms

questions.question: A corpus is dominated by queries containing exact invoice IDs. Which design judgment is strongest?

Use only dense similarity regardless of evaluation
Expand each identifier into every nearby number

questions.question: Which evaluation best establishes that vocabulary mismatch harms candidate generation?
options: Count the number of words in the corpus
Measure labeled recall at a cutoff by query segment
Visualize one pair of embeddings
Inspect only successful exact-match queries
